name: Ina Garten
about: Hosted Barefoot Contessa on Food Network since 2002. Known for simple, reliable home cooking.

name: Giada De Laurentiis
about: Le Cordon Bleu Paris graduate. Hosted Everyday Italian and runs the Giadzy recipe site.

name: Bobby Flay
about: Iron Chef and host of Beat Bobby Flay. Founded Mesa Grill in New York.

name: Anne Burrell
about: Culinary Institute of America graduate. Hosted Secrets of a Restaurant Chef and Worst Cooks in America.

name: Alex Guarnaschelli
about: Iron Chef and Chopped judge. Executive chef at Butter in New York.

name: Michael Symon
about: Iron Chef and James Beard Best Chef winner. Chef-owner of Lola in Cleveland.

name: Gordon Ramsay
about: Chef-owner of Restaurant Gordon Ramsay in London, which holds three Michelin stars.

name: Jamie Oliver
about: Trained at London's River Café before The Naked Chef. Big on quick, fresh home cooking.

name: Tom Colicchio
about: Head judge on Top Chef. Co-founded Gramercy Tavern and founded Craft in New York.

name: Stephanie Izard
about: Won Top Chef season 4. Chef-owner of Girl & the Goat in Chicago.

name: Missy Robbins
about: Chef-owner of Lilia and Misi in Brooklyn, two of New York's best-loved pasta restaurants.

name: Massimo Bottura
about: Chef of Osteria Francescana in Modena, twice named the world's best restaurant.

name: Lidia Bastianich
about: Chef-owner of Felidia in New York and host of Lidia's Kitchen on PBS.

name: J. Kenji López-Alt
about: Author of The Food Lab and longtime culinary director of Serious Eats. Explains the why behind each step.

name: Jacques Pépin
about: Cooked for three French heads of state, then taught America technique on PBS for decades. James Beard Lifetime Achievement winner.

name: Thomas Keller
about: Chef of The French Laundry in Napa and Per Se in New York, both with three Michelin stars.

name: José Andrés
about: Brought Spanish tapas to America. Runs minibar in Washington, D.C. and founded World Central Kitchen.

name: Nancy Silverton
about: Founded La Brea Bakery and co-owns Pizzeria and Osteria Mozza in Los Angeles.

name: Marcus Samuelsson
about: Chef-owner of Red Rooster in Harlem. Won Top Chef Masters and judges on Chopped.

name: Kristen Kish
about: Won Top Chef season 10 and now hosts the show.

name: Richard Blais
about: Won Top Chef: All-Stars. Known for playful, science-minded cooking.

name: Alton Brown
about: Created Good Eats, the show that explains the science of cooking. Won a James Beard award for it.

name: Emeril Lagasse
about: Chef-owner of Emeril's in New Orleans. Brought Creole and Cajun cooking to American TV.

name: Masaharu Morimoto
about: Iron Chef on both the original Japanese show and Iron Chef America. Runs the Morimoto restaurants.

name: Maneet Chauhan
about: Chopped judge and chef-owner of Chauhan Ale & Masala House in Nashville. Cooks bold, modern Indian food.

name: Jose Garces
credential: Iron Chef, James Beard Best Chef
about: Iron Chef and James Beard Best Chef Mid-Atlantic. Known for Spanish and Latin cooking in Philadelphia.

name: Aarón Sánchez
about: Chopped judge and chef behind Johnny Sánchez in New Orleans. Cooks modern Mexican food.

name: Geoffrey Zakarian
about: Iron Chef and Chopped judge, with a long career in New York fine dining.

name: Scott Conant
about: Chopped judge and founder of Scarpetta, famous for its spaghetti with tomato and basil.

name: Yotam Ottolenghi
about: Chef-owner of the Ottolenghi delis and ROVI in London. Famous for bold, vegetable-led Middle Eastern cooking.

name: Rick Bayless
about: Won the first Top Chef Masters and James Beard Outstanding Chef. Chef-owner of Frontera Grill and Topolobampo in Chicago.

name: Eric Ripert
about: Chef of Le Bernardin in New York, which has held three Michelin stars since the guide came to the city.

name: Andrew Zimmern
about: Host of Bizarre Foods and a four-time James Beard award winner. Cooks food from all over the world.

name: Nigella Lawson
about: Author of How to Eat and host of Nigella Bites and Nigella Express. Generous, unfussy home cooking.
